claim.why_it_matters: Two independent lead-in sentences from two different printed pages are concatenated into one run-on line, and the page-400 sentence is filed under the '## Page 399' heading. The result reads as a single cross-reference ('...Entry-name clause where screen-attribute-clauses is:'), which mis-states what 13.18.20 covers, orphans the screen-attribute-clauses figure on page 400 from its introducing sentence, and breaks page attribution for anyone following a page cross-reference.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides at 300 dpi. PDF page 399 (printed page 369, ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E), 13.17.2 screen description entry, Format 2 (elementary)): after the Format-2 syntax figure the page ends with exactly one body line, 'where entry-name-clause is described in 13.18.20, Entry-name clause'. Nothing follows it before the footer ('(c)ISO/IEC 2023 369'). It is a complete, standalone sentence (no trailing period in the printed text, consistent with the sibling occurrence at markdown line 21210). PDF page 400 (printed page 370): after the running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', the first body line is 'where screen-attribute-clauses is:', followed by the screen-attribute-clauses figure (BELL / BLINK / HIGHLIGHT-LOWLIGHT / REVERSE-VIDEO / UNDERLINE / FOREGROUND-COLOR / BACKGROUND-COLOR), then 'where picture-clause is described in 13.18.40, PICTURE clause.', then 'where source-destination-clauses is:' with its figure, then '13.17.3 Syntax rules'. So the two sentences are unambiguously on two different printed pages, separated by a page boundary and a running header. Markdown: line 17157 is a single line reading 'where entry-name-clause is described in 13.18.20, Entry-name clause where screen-attribute-clauses is:' and it sits above the '' / '## Page 400' boundary, i.e. inside the Page 399 slice. The Page 400 slice then opens with the running header and goes straight into the fenced screen-attribute-clauses figure with no lead-in sentence of its own. Ruled out the standard refutations: this is not reflow, wrapping, hyphenation, or page-break furniture. `grep -n 'where screen-attribute-clauses is' specs/ISO_COBOL.md` returns exactly one hit -- line 17157 -- so there is no second, correctly-placed copy on page 400; the sentence exists only in its merged form. The merge is not a harmless soft-wrap join either: the two sentences are separated in the PDF by a page break, a footer, and a header, and the join removes the sentence boundary, producing a grammatically valid but factually wrong single cross-reference that appears to say 13.18.20 is 'where screen-attribute-clauses is'. Meaning is therefore changed, and the screen-attribute-clauses figure loses its introducer.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED, and the claim is accurate as written. Precise form: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 17157 concatenates two sentences that the PDF prints on separate pages -- 'where entry-name-clause is described in 13.18.20, Entry-name clause' (last body line of PDF page 399 / printed 369, closing 13.17.2 Format 2) and 'where screen-attribute-clauses is:' (first body line of PDF page 400 / printed 370, introducing the screen-attribute-clauses figure). Two aggravating details worth recording: (a) the merged line is the ONLY occurrence of 'where screen-attribute-clauses is' in the entire markdown, so the page-400 figure has no lead-in sentence anywhere -- the '## Page 400' slice opens directly with the fenced figure; and (b) the merged sentence is grammatically well-formed, so the corruption is silent to a reader and misattributes the content of 13.18.20. Fix: split into two lines and move 'where screen-attribute-clauses is:' below the '' / '## Page 400' boundary, immediately above the screen-attribute-clauses fence, matching the sibling pattern already correct for 'where picture-clause is described in 13.18.40, PICTURE clause.' and 'where source-destination-clauses is:'.
